summary: Give loop rounds the answers of their exit gates, end a loop that makes no progress with a verdict, and stop retrying a loop that has already stopped

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes. The reconciler reads the loop.state claims it already writes; a loop that stopped before this change is judged by the same final loop.state claim.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. New loop outcome documents use the existing document store and the existing feedback field of loop.state.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention, authority or admission rule change and no rules-version change.

compatibility.detail: Adds the optional stop rule no-progress N (2 to 100) to loop stop blocks. A node that runs older code refuses to apply a mission that declares it from KDL, but a mission revision that reaches it already stored deserializes with the unknown field ignored, so an older node that runs such a loop goes on to max-rounds while upgraded nodes stop at the rule: the rule is reliable only once every member that can run the mission is upgraded. Missions that do not declare it are unaffected. The feedback a round receives through loop.feedback now refers to doc/loop-feedback/LOOP/ROUND/outcome, which records the keep or discard decision, the metrics and each exit gate's answer. Behavior fix: a loop whose on-exhausted outcome is fail and that stopped on a stop rule before its last round is no longer retried as a new attempt, so stop rules now stop the loop; its step stays failed and the run fails. Exhaustion verdicts name the failing exit gates.

downtime.detail: No startup work or expected interruption; no migration.

manual.detail: No operator actions or configuration changes are required. A loop that wants the no-progress verdict declares stop { no-progress N }.

recovery.detail: No persistent state changes or new swap-back restrictions. An older node ignores the outcome documents and retries a stopped loop as before.
